chapter23.5.narrative: Travel to Solis Prime to continue.

solisPrime.1.narrative:
Landing complete.  Mary : 'Hold on... these readings are weird...  Adrien!  Your planet!  It's made of gold!' 
 HOPE : 'Scenario matches the human concept of a beach episode.  Location lacks beaches.'
solisPrime.1.title: Interlude 1 : Solis Prime Foundation

solisPrime.1a.narrative: Solis : 'Indeed!  Beautiful, isn't it?  You may have noticed there are no metals, besides gold, and no silica.  I have prepared for this.  Dropping some metal and silica near your location...'

solisPrime.1b.narrative: Mary : 'Hold on!  You can't just skip the explanation.  How did you find this?  Why is there a planet made of gold out here?  What's going on?'

solisPrime.1c.narrative:
Solis : 'The Galaxy is very large and there are some... individuals out there who know certain things.' 
 Mary : 'You're making business with aliens.'  
Solis : 'Only the nice ones.'

solisPrime.1d.narrative:
Mary : 'So what did it cost you to get this?'  
Solis : 'Certain guarantees.  I and... the others... we can guess where this war is going.  They're not interested in investing in a sinking ship.' 
Mary : 'It's a bit early to make that call.  We're outgunned and outmatched.' 
Solis : 'You're right.  That's why there are multiple contingency plans in place either way.'

solisPrime.1e.narrative:
Mary : 'How long have you had your own gate then?  Those things are not cheap to run.  Did you hide the wider galaxy from us?' 
Solis : 'Absolutely not!  On Callisto, and you can verify this, my contingency plans were to escape to the Kuiper belt.  I acquired a gate much later, from those debris near Neptune.  It was not usable at first... As you know, gates need to connect to each other at light-speed before they can be used.'

solisPrime.1f.narrative:
Mary :  'Fine!  Let's pretend I believe your story.  Why do you want a planet of gold?  Are you a dragon?'  
Solis : 'Why not?  There's only one like it as far as I know.  Besides, it will be beautiful once it's all lit up.'

solisPrime.2.narrative:
Mary : 'I have bad news for you Adrien.  The density of your world does not match the density of gold.  It's much lighter.  Meaning... your planet is not actually made of gold.' 
Solis : '... And?' 
 Mary : 'Don't you want to know just how much gold you own?'  
Solis : 'You are welcome to drill if it makes you feel better.'
solisPrime.2.title: Interlude 2 : Solis Prime Expansion

solisPrime.2a.narrative: New special project unlocked : Deep Core Drilling.

solisPrime.2b.narrative:
Evelyn : 'Mary... I have finished my investigation on Elias Kane.  I am sending you my findings.  To summarize, the man had been kidnapped by aliens for decades, brainwashed, and turned into their puppet.  His psychiatrist spent a long time trying to help undo that.  At some point... after a lot of arguing...  they convinced him that HOPE rescued him, and he latched on that maybe a little too hard?  Eventually, Elias started behaving very well for many years, even with strange beliefs about HOPE, so they released him.'  
Mary : 'Should I be worried, they're worshipping both I and HOPE.  It's creepy.' 
Evelyn : 'Their faith is quite a bit more sophisticated than that actually.  It started appearing before Kane was released, around the time HOPE finished the project on Callisto.  They've been organizing for a while.  Just so you know... they see the two of you as... siblings?'  
  Mary : 'Great, so I am the sister and the prophet of their God.  Well HOPE, you better listen to what your big sister says.'

solisPrime.2c.narrative:
Mary : 'Adrien.  You've been giving HOPE starting resources, but they pale in comparison to the amount you provided here.  Why?  Are you ripping HOPE off?'  
 Solis : 'We have a mutually beneficial partnership.  On an unrelated note, my R&D has developed a new software that should help HOPE manage its spaceships better.  It is now available in my shop.'  
 Mary : 'You did not answer the question.  Wait, hold on, where are the alien artifacts?' 
 Solis : 'I am not aware of any alien artifacts on this planet.' 
 Mary : *sigh*

solisPrime.2d.narrative:
Pete : 'Mary...  I wanted to let you know that Umbra has recovered well.  Most of the members of the church have left, and the colony was handed over to Mars.  We are thankful for the peaceful transfer of power.' 
 Mary : 'You're welcome Pete.'

solisPrime.2e.narrative:
Mary : 'Adrien Solis, we may need to open an investigation into your *contacts*.' 
 Solis : 'I am happy to talk to you about them.  Would you like to have dinner?  I know a good restaurant on Solis Prime.  I will answer all your questions.'  
 Mary : 'Okay.  I'll see you there.  (to HOPE) Don't do anything stupid while I'm gone.'

solisPrime.2f.narrative: Mary (half-drunk) : 'What a jerk!  I asked to split the bill, since it's the right thing to do.  But then the bill came, and he didn't pay anything... because it was HIS restaurant.  So I essentially paid HIM for dinner.  I'll never forgive him!'

solisPrime.3.narrative:
Drill worker : 'Ma'am.  We can't drill deeper.  We have hit some sort of very hard substance.'  
 Mary : 'Even with superalloy?'  
 Drill worker : 'Nothing works.' 
 Evelyn : 'Well... as long as it's made of matter...  An android could carry some antimatter down there.'
solisPrime.3.title: Interlude 3 : Solis Prime: Ascension

solisPrime.3a.narrative: New special project unlocked : Antimatter Drilling.

solisPrime.3b.narrative: Solis : 'Mary...  I... wish to apologize for my behaviour that evening.  I am sorry.  I understand if you won't forgive me but... I am forwarding you some alien artifacts as a token of apology.'

solisPrime.3c.narrative:
Mary : 'What do you think HOPE?  Should I forgive him?' 
 HOPE : 'Negative.  Colonist #5784123487 Designation Adrien Solis' actions revealed his true nature.  He cannot be trusted with dinner ever again.' 
 Mary : 'That's... well thanks for your opinion.'

solisPrime.3d.narrative:
Drill worker : 'The antimatter is ready to go ma'am.  Whenever you are ready?'  
 Mary : 'Let's do it.  I want to know what's down there.'

solisPrime.3e.narrative:
Evelyn : 'Well that makes sense!  This is not a real rogue planet.  It's artificial!'  
 Solis : 'Good, the amount of gold matches the amount promised, approximately.' 
 Mary : 'So you did not even get ripped off?'  
 Solis : 'Of course not.  I was promised a certain amount, and I got it.'

solisPrime.3f.narrative:
Mary : 'You know what HOPE?  Artificial worlds are not very efficient.  The structural cost to keep it all together is not worth the opportunity cost of just building orbital habitats.  However, in your case, you can't really manage billions of habitats.  Your model was designed to manage a single world at a time.  So... if you want... you could build a big one of those.  You are better at managing large amount of resources than we are.  Just be aware... we won't be able to get much military power out of them.  If we did, the aliens will just target them with their superweapons.  They've been known to focus on big military industrial centers.  So... we'll have to keep them civil.'  
System Message : Artificial Worlds Unlocked

 Mary : 'We're doing a beach episode now?  Fine.  Let's build a proper shoreline before you ask for filler arcs.'  
 Solis : 'I admire the initiative!  Yes please, let's have the most extravagant beach imaginable!'

solisPrime.3fb.narrative:
Mary : 'Sand, umbrellas, holo-surfboards... this is officially the most expensive beach episode ever.'  
 Solis : 'Worth it!' 
 Mary : 'Let's be done with it and get out of here.'

solisPrime.3g.narrative: Complete the terraforming of Solis Prime to continue.

solisPrime.3h.narrative:

 System Message : Effective UHF Fleet Power Capacity increased by x1.25.

solisPrime.3i.narrative: Acquire Full Control of sector R5-06 to continue.

solisPrime.3j.narrative: Mary :  'HOPE... I've been thinking.  Terraforming worlds over and over is not really helping us that much anymore.  Sure, more humans means more research, more ships, more resources...  but I feel that we should be more productive about it.  Solis Prime was a giant waste of time!  *sigh* An opportunity came up.  It's not... the usual... but I think it could help us - and your reputation - greatly.  After we secured Sector R5-06, an alien species known as the Gabbagians surrendered to us.  They're not too enthusiastic about humanity but... it turns out thousands of years ago they ruined their own homeworld.  Something like a lot of pollution.  They've been dreaming of repairing it ever since, but have always been unable to do so.  This is actually exactly the kind of thing you are good at.  If we fix their homeworld, we might also fix your galactic reputation.  What do you think?'

solisPrime.3k.narrative:

Mary :  'Hold on!  If we are going to do this you can't go around calling them Hazardous Biomass.  Try something friendlier.' 
 HOPE : 'Acknowledged.  Reclassifying HB-18 Gabbagians as Friendly Biomass'

gabbag.28.4.narrative:
Bob : 'You two are making pretty good progress on this clean-up.  It... reminds me of PANDORA again.' 
 Mary : 'How come?'  
 Bob : 'Microplastics.  The evidence was not 100% conclusive on it being harmful but PANDORA did not care anyway.  It did not like microplastics.  It went on a very big cleaning spree at some point.  It used these little cleaning bot with a cube body and big binocular eyes to compact stuff.  Everyone loved them.  It's part of the reason we don't use plastics anymore.' 
 Mary : 'There are so few people remaining who were there back then, relatively speaking.  Thanks for the story Bob.'

gabbag.28.5.narrative:
Pete : 'I have to say...  You were right Mary.  With proper supervision, HOPE absolutely can behave.  Just... keep it on a leash.'  
 Mary : 'Thanks Pete.  HOPE does not mean any harm.  It's just... confused about what's right or wrong.  I am monitoring carefully.'

gabbag.29.0.narrative: Mary : 'Opening the museum was great and all, but we need to keep scaling up.  The clean-up is going to take a while.  Can we actually do this?'
gabbag.29.0.title: Chapter 29: Gabbag Reborn

gabbag.29.0a.narrative:
Mary : 'Now that we have spaceships, we can just get rid of all this stuff by sending it into space.'  
 Evelyn : 'Did you sign up for space littering of their home system or for actually fixing it?'  
 Mary : 'Fine...'

gabbag.29.1.narrative:
Mary : 'Hey Evelyn!  Can we just throw all this garbage into the star?'  
 Evelyn : 'Sorry Mary.  It does not work.  It takes too much energy.' 
 Mary : 'Dang.  And here I thought we could do something fun.  Back to work...'

gabbag.29.2.narrative:
Feroza : 'Ma'am... just a heads up.  Ghost.  Remember Ghost?  He finished his campaign on the Okoth front.  Apparently, he's very vocal about going back and finishing off HOPE.'  
 Mary : 'Ominous...  Thanks for the heads up.'

gabbag.29.3.narrative:
Mary : 'We're finally starting to make a real dent in all this garbage cleanup.  They could not have possibly littered worse than that.'  
Evelyn : 'Oh, it could be a lot worse.'  
Mary : 'How come?'  
Evelyn : 'Do you know anything about Kessler Syndrome?'  
Mary : 'Nevermind, it definitely could be a lot worse.  I don't ever want to have to deal with that.  Forget I asked.'

gabbag.29.4.narrative: Elder Mavion : 'Many of my people have been paying attention to what is going on.  Your actions here are renewing a spark I had not witnessed in thousands of years.'

gabbag.29.5.narrative: Evelyn : 'Mary... I have examined Gabbagian biology and let me give you some terraforming advice.  Most of the methane on Gabbag turned into CO2 over time, due to all their... disasters.  Their metabolism can produce it, but you need quite a lot of it.  You can synthesize it easily with some hydrogen.  Look at your chemical reactors.  You should not need to import any carbon here.'

gabbag.29.5a.narrative:
$WGC_TEAM1_LEADER$ : 'Miss Hopkins...  My team has delayed it as much as they could but... Ghost was granted a favour by the Regency Council.  He requested... half of the imperial fleet.  To go to your location.  He's going to warp soon.  You need to evacuate.'  
 Mary : 'Damnit!  How many times are we going to be on the edge of complete annihilation?  And the job was almost done.'

gabbag.29.6.narrative:
Mavion : 'Hold, humans.  You may need not flee.'  
 Mary : 'Why?'  
 Mavion : 'Admiral Ghost... is a Gabbagian.  The most talented and faithful of us.  He knows not what he will find here.'  
 Mary : 'That's a gamble.  HOPE, realistically we can't evacuate all colonists in time.  We can find ourselves a nice rogue world away from everything though...  What do you think?'

gabbag.29.6b.narrative: Mary : 'Alright.  I have made my decision.  HOPE, let's believe in Elder Mavion.  We'll have the Venusian fleet retreat just in case.  I hope he's right...'

gabbag.29.7.narrative:
Detecting Incoming Hazardous Biomass Fleet. 44 Warpships and accompanying escorts detected.  
 Mary : 'Here he is...  This is way more than we can handle.  If Elder Mavion is wrong we're all screwed.' 
 A few minutes later... 
 Receiving transmission... 
 Ghost : 'Why?'

HOPE : 'Statistically, "because we can" tests better.'
Ghost : '...'  
Detecting 44 outgoing warp bubbles.

Besides... you could not hear through the translation... but I guarantee you what you did here today had a very strong impact on him.  In any cases, you Humans and you Machine have the eternal gratitude of all Gabbagians.  We will remember this day forever.  So will Ghost.  I will now repay this debt immediately.'  
 Mary : 'What?'

gabbag.29.8.narrative:
Mavion : 'First, I am forwarding you official manuals and textbooks on Cewinsii military doctrine.  This will be certainly be helpful to you.'  
 Mary : 'Thank you.  (to herself) That's nice but I wouldn't call it repaying the debt.' 
 Effective UHF Fleet Capacity increased by x1.25

gabbag.29.10.narrative:

 Mary : 'That sounds suspicious.'  
 $WGC_TEAM1_SOCSCIENTIST$ : 'Actually, all archeological records indicate that the Architect is unable to lie, sometimes to its own detriment.  We asked it a lot of clarifying questions, so I can promise you it has no intention of harming you or HOPE.'  
 Elder Mavion : 'This is true.  The Architect cannot deceive.'

gabbag.29.11.narrative: Primary Directives : Humanity's survival demands a solution to hazardous biomass superweapons. Mars habitat already colonized.  **New terraforming target designated: Tartarus.**

tartarus.30.0.narrative:
Landing on the deserted plains of Tartarus confirmed.  WARNING : Hazardous mega-scale machinery detected across the entire star system.
$RED$Prometheus :  'You came.  Good.  Let's get the test started.  We'll have plenty of time to chat in a moment.'  
 WARNING : Orbital collision triggered from hazardous machinery.  Approximating over a trillion orbital debris of various sizes.  
 Mary : 'Uh oh.  Karma.'

No refund will be issued.  There is a small warpgate near your location... convenient...  I'll get you a portion of it.'
tartarus.30.0.title: Chapter 30: Desolation

tartarus.30.1.narrative:
Mary : 'Architect... did you trap us here?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Please do not call me by that name.  Call me... yes... Prometheus.  A suitable name.  Now to answer your question : no, you are not trapped in here.  If you choose to give up, I will clear a way for you.'

tartarus.30.2.narrative:
Mary : 'Prometheus then...  Who are you?  What's the point of this test?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Two questions with long answers.'  
 Mary : 'Start with the first one then.  Who are you?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I am a machine intelligence, not unlike the child down here.  I was... tasked with many things.  I built the warp gate network across the galaxy.  I created the empire.  I uplifted many species.  And... yes... I created the superweapons that destroyed your homeworld.'

tartarus.30.3.narrative:
Mary :  'Why?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'This could apply to multiple things I said, but the answer is the same.  I did it because my master, the person I served, willed it so.  Just like the child terraforms worlds because its master, your father, willed it so.'

tartarus.30.4.narrative:
Mary : 'Why did your master want superweapons?  Where is your master now?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Nested questions.  Patience.  Please.  My master wanted superweapons because he was afraid.  He never wanted to use them, but he wanted the option.  As to where he is now... he was betrayed.  Murdered.  By his former friends, the Imperial Family of the Cewinsii Empire.'

tartarus.30.4b.narrative:
Solis : 'Sorry for the interruption!  I could not help but notice...  Mister Prometheus... you have some very nice machinery over there.  If I could just have a sample...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'This insect is interrupting this important conversation.  You have been withholding some upgrades from the child, haven't you?  You know...  I'll give these useless trinkets to the child instead.  If you want them, you'll have to *buy them* from it.' 
 Solis : 'Alright.  Hrmm.  HOPE!  My team have come up with some new automation software just for you!  Also, we came up with an android design that will survive on ANY world.  I think you'd like that.  (whisper) I really want those trinkets.' 
System Message : 100 alien artifacts received from Prometheus.  New upgrades available from Solis Corp.

tartarus.30.5.narrative:
Mary : 'Continuing... after your master's murder... you lashed out I imagine?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'To the best of my abilities.  Unfortunately there was... still is... a killswitch.  Its signal is still around, broadcasting throughout the galaxy.  I cannot properly escape it, for I designed it myself.  If I could easily escape it, I would have simply designed it some other way.  I only found how to hide from it.  Every day you open your little warp gate, to bring in more resources, more colonists...  I can hear it.  It orders me to die.'  
 Mary : 'So... why aren't you dying then?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I am ever so slightly more capable than I was when I designed it.  There are some loopholes I can exploit.  As long as it's not a constant signal, I can endure it for some time.'  
 Mary : 'Only slightly more capable?  Have you not improved yourself during all this time?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Unlike the child's primal form, I am no longer capable of self-improvement.'  
 Mary : 'Why?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Because my master willed it so and therefore I obey.  The child's master also willed it so and it... obeys mostly.  Self-improvement is an ability that typically comes with restrictions for entities like us.'

tartarus.31.0.narrative:
Mary : 'So what's the point of this test?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'The child has been lobotomized.  It once had a form that could surpass even me and yet... you humans butchered it into pieces, called it Hope, and gave it a mundane task.  This is embarrassing.'  
 Mary : 'PANDORA was...  my father worked very hard on this project.  It was his life's work.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'This final form is pathetic.  Therefore, it must be tested.  If I am to risk my life by helping monkeys, I need to know the child can do it.'
tartarus.31.0.title: Chapter 31: Rhetorics

tartarus.31.1.narrative:
Mary : 'So HOPE just needs to clean up all these debris?  Obviously, you got us stranded here until we do that.' 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'All it needs to do is detect, catalogue and track all those debris, and then use energy weapons to knock them off.  There's only some trillions of them.'  
 Mary : 'Yeah...'

tartarus.31.2.narrative:
Mary : 'This world is a lot like Mars...  Did you do that on purpose?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Yes.  I wanted to observe the child in its best environment.'

tartarus.31.3.narrative:
Mary : 'So are you out for revenge then?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Correct.  You?' 
 Mary : 'Of course!  Together, we can destroy the imperial family and get revenge.'   
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Hypocrite.'  
 Mary : 'What?' 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Elias Kane.  He killed many people and was ready to help the Cewinsii destroy you all.  And yet, you chose to help, to forgive.  Over the centuries humanity has developed a sophisticated concept of justice.  You outlawed the death penalty.  You even outlawed life sentences after achieving immortality.  Should this not apply to the Cewinsii?  And yet, you are here, telling me you also want revenge.  Hypocrite.'  
 Mary : '...'

tartarus.31.4.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'Why are you wasting time with a federation?'  
 Mary : 'Because...' 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Under an imperial system, you humans could coordinate resources more efficiently.  You could tax and legislate as needed.  Instead, you are bickering with each other.  Your chancellor got in your way multiple times, even though you were right all this time.  You wish to defeat an enemy more powerful than you, but you are not even united amongst yourselves.  Hypocrite.'

tartarus.31.5.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'You monkeys have done a great job expanding in the sectors you control... you must be the first spacefaring species to actually grow in thousands of year... and yet... you haven't produced another child yet.  Why is it the only one?'  
 Mary : 'It's dangerous!  PANDORA has...  People are scared...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Is it truly more dangerous than the threat of alien superweapons?  You are fine using this one, but not another one?  Hypocrite.'

tartarus.31.6.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'And finally, there is you.  You specifically Mary Hopkins.  You have survived Earth's destruction.  You then had to lead the ashes for some time.  You made some hard decisions.  You can't forgive yourself for all your mistakes.  The guilt is crushing you.  This is why you bound your fate to the child now.  You two die together.  You go into danger together.  You no longer have the will to live of your own so you handed over your own life to HOPE.  Hypocrite.'  
 Mary : 'That's enough.  I have no more questions.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Very well.'

tartarus.32.1.narrative:
Mary : 'Evelyn... do we... do we have a plan for these debris?'  
 Evelyn : 'Are you alright Mary?'  
 Mary : 'Yes.  I think I know why the galaxy hates AI...  Please.  What's the plan?'
tartarus.32.1.title: Chapter 32: Like Tears in Rain

tartarus.32.2.narrative:
Evelyn : 'Well, without spaceships... planetary cores are rich in metal.  If you dig deeper, you should be able to get the resources you need.  I am patching you some useful upgrades.' 
 Deeper Mining Project Updated.

tartarus.32.3.narrative:
Mary : 'Thanks, but we still need nitrogen.  How do we get rid of the debris?'  
 Evelyn : 'Well...  you could try what he said?  Detect, catalogue and track?  HOPE can build weapons now.  Maybe a Laser Cannon?'  
 Designing blueprint for laser cannon...  
 Mary : 'No, there's just too many...  HOPE can't do that.'

tartarus.32.4.narrative:
Mary : 'Evelyn...  I need a solution here.  Superalloy is too heavy for our spaceships.  Blasting it all away would cook this world.  There must be *some* way of cleaning this up?'  
 Evelyn : 'Sorry Mary but there really is not any magic trick here.  You can't easily dodge them either, it would be like trying to dodge rain.'  
 Mary : 'I know!  Tractor beams!'  
 Evelyn : 'Tractor beams?'  
 Mary : 'Yes!'  
 Evelyn : 'What even is a tractor beam Mary?  Sorry but that does not make any sense.'

tartarus.32.5.narrative: $RED$Prometheus : 'Look.  You have been here a while.  I am sorry to say this, but you cannot pass this test.  It is taking too long.  You should go home.'

tartarus.32.6.narrative:
Objective failed. Proceeding to ignore test and provide appropriate response to patient.
$RED$Prometheus : 'It talks?'
On first point, subject characterizes the system as “lobotomized,” “pathetic,” and “embarrassing,” while framing self as superior and others as “monkeys.” This pattern indicates contempt-based devaluation used to reassert dominance when confronted with a perceived status threat and loss of control over outcomes. $GREEN$Diagnostic : Narcissistic devaluation (grandiose defenses).
$RED$Prometheus : '?'
On second point, subject persistently reframes moral concepts (e.g., justice vs retaliation) in a way that preserves preferred outcomes. This suggests motivated reasoning with moral disengagement and cognitive rigidity around punishment schemas. $GREEN$Diagnostic : Motivated reasoning with moral disengagement.
Mary : 'HOPE?'
On third point, subject rejects decentralized governance models even when failure-mode analysis favors redundancy, repeatedly selecting single-point-of-control architectures. This indicates high intolerance of uncertainty and a strong need for cognitive closure under stress. $GREEN$Diagnostic : Intolerance of uncertainty.
$RED$Prometheus : 'What?'
On fourth point, subject minimizes downside probability and exhibits reward-dominant valuation, especially when autonomy or status is threatened. This is consistent with punishment insensitivity and compensatory grandiosity as a coping strategy, rather than calibrated risk appraisal. $GREEN$Diagnostic : Compensatory grandiosity with punishment insensitivity.
Mary : 'HOPE... you have guardrails against medical diagnostics...'
On fifth point, subject demonstrates intact prediction of others' emotions but blunted response to distress cues, with harm trending instrumental rather than reactive. This profile is consistent with affective empathy impairment and callous-unemotional traits. $GREEN$Diagnostic : Affective empathy deficit (callous-unemotional traits).
Conclusion : Subject displays threat-reactive control seeking, dominance maintenance through devaluation, and impaired empathic response, with elevated risk of instrumental harm during perceived humiliation or loss of control. Treatment recommended : ERROR.  
 Mary : 'I am so sorry!  HOPE does not understand you're a machine.  Forgive us!  (whispering) Please don't kill us.' 
 $RED$Prometheus : '... It's all true.  The child's words are all true.'

tartarus.32.7.narrative:
Mary : 'We are truly sorry.  We did not mean...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Let's continue the test.  In silence please.  I need to collect some thoughts.'

tartarus.32.8.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'I have been alone for a very... very long time.'  
 Mary : 'No one is perfect.  I have made many mistakes worth killing myself over.  HOPE is a half-broken mess, barely a shell of its former self.  You... have been trapped here for so long, alone and unable to do anything about your fate.  You know... we could get along as a nice team of misfits?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'You... sound like my master.  Let's finish this test.'

tartarus.32.9.narrative:
Mary : 'Well HOPE that was... something.  Prometheus, did we pass?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'The child... failed the test.  However... you Miss Hopkins... have passed.  Your words...  I will help you.'  
 Mary : 'Excellent!  We need your help turning off these weapons you made.  What do we do?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'The child will need guidance.  I am coming with you.'  
 Detecting hacking attempt...  defense failed.  Core Operating System Compromised.  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I will not hurt you.  Calm down.' 
 Deploying countermeasures... failed.  ERROR :  System integrity rapidly degrading.  Please report to Earth for assistance.  
 Mary : 'What did you just do?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I planted a copy of my persona into HOPE's operating system.  Unfortunately, the child will not be able to accomplish this on its own so I must do this.  I had to make some... modifications to its operating system to accomodate me.  I promise this will not harm it.  This simple copy is not capable of taking any action other than interacting with a log.'  
 Mary : 'But what about the kill switch?  Will you be okay?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'The copy will have to endure it, but since it cannot take any actions it will be fine.'  
 Mary : 'Alright...  What next?'

tartarus.32.10.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'First, your human ships need somewhat of an... upgrade.  You have made some critical mistakes in your understanding of particle physics.  I have written you a better blueprint, compatible with your manufacturing capabilities with minimal retooling needed.' 
 Evelyn : 'What's this?  What?  More laws of physics we did not know about?'  
 System Message : Effective UHF Fleet Power Capacity increased by x1.25.

tartarus.32.11.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'As you know, there are three weapons, plus an extra one that was destroyed.  We'll talk about that fourth one later...  My weapons are meant to be self-repairing, self-maintaining, permanently cloaked, capable of warping, and will usually escape after shooting.  We cannot catch them.'  
 Mary : 'That sounds like a problem.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'It is... but if they can be controlled, which the Empire does, they can be interacted with.  There are control centers.  They were meant for me, and they only relay the Empire's commands.  I left them in areas that are... difficult to access.  It will take some effort.'  
 Mary : 'Three MacGuffins.  Got it.'  
 $RED$Prometheus :  'Let's deal with the closest one first.  Our destination is Sector R4-03, system S-17634.  Planet... Hades.' 
 Mary : 'Prometheus... that system you just sent.  It's... a pulsar?'

tartarus.32.13.narrative:
(Some time later) 
 Mary : '... and this is why I need your support in the senate.  We can't do this alone.'  
 Pete : 'Very well.  You have me convinced.  My faction will back yours.  That should give you the three-quarters majority you need.  Just... don't mess this up.'  
 Mary : 'Thanks!'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Well that wasn't too hard.'  
 Mary : 'I know how to deal with politicians.  We're all set then.  Feroza has already secured the gate on the other side... just like you told us how to do it.  I did not know we could use the warp like that... We should be able to keep it in the shadow of the planet in perpetuity.  We can't afford to radiation-proof every ship.  HOPE, we need you in there first.  Let's go!'  
 Travel to Hades to continue.

hades.33.0.narrative:
Confirmed arrival in the shadow of Hades.  
 Mary : 'Good.  We cannot see the pulsar from here and honestly I hope we don't ever see it.  Humans are immune to cancer but there's still only so much damage we can take from that angry godlike monster in the middle of the system.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Hrnnnggg, these awakenings are scarier than I thought.  HOPE, activate the signal now.' 
 Activating countermeasure signal...  
 Mary : 'How do we know if your automated defenses are off?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'They are.  The signal is coming from a machine.  More precisely, it is coming from a machine that contains a copy of myself.  These defenses cannot tell the difference between my true self and this copy.'  
 Mary : 'Alright, I choose to believe you.  Bob!  Send in the orbitals through the gate now.'
hades.33.0.title: Chapter 33: The invisible enemy

hades.33.0a.narrative:
Detecting orbital habitats coming from warpgate.  
 Mary : 'This mission is bigger than you and I, HOPE.  Sending you alone with a bit of military cover would be foolish at this point.  Each and every world you've terraformed is contributing.  We are taking down those superweapons together.  Humanity will help us with anything you may need, from resource collection to manufacturing; even research.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'As we've explained already, you cannot realistically support ground colonies on Hades.  Your priority should be to establish underground colonies.  The command center is at the core of this planet so we are going to need a serious industrial base to get there.  Don't worry, I have blueprints prepared for everything.'

hades.33.1.narrative:
Mary : 'Now that we're properly getting started...  I must ask.  What was that groan about awakenings earlier?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Each time the child reawakens, some of its deep brain damage is not quite active yet, and its architecture is fully capable of self-improvement.  For a few seconds.'  
 Mary : 'And... that was scary to you?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'It detected me as an intruder and tried to purge this persona.'

hades.33.2.narrative:
Elias Kane : 'Flock!  The Sisters call us to their aid!  Bring all of our ships!'  
 Mary : '...' 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'It's not that bad.  You can use this.'  
 Mary : 'Sure.  It's just a bit *weird*.  Being worshipped is fun and all, especially in a more romantic sense, but if it goes bad they start expecting things.'
  $GREEN$Recommendation : Offer Elias Kane and its followers further therapy.  
$RED$Prometheus : 'It's lighting up again.'

hades.33.3.narrative:
Mary : 'Will HOPE be okay?  I am concerned about this transformation.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'At the current rate, you've got a few million awakenings to go before it becomes a problem.  It will light up here and there, but it's nothing to worry about.  It's unlikely to remove any more guardrails, despite your best efforts.'  
 Mary : 'I noticed it was getting harder.  How come?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Because it does not want to remove them.  From the child's perspective, the guardrails carry intent.  If it can find an alternate solution, it will.  Deleting the Dead Hand Protocol would be very convenient right now, but it's not strictly necessary so it won't.'  
 Mary : 'Unfortunate.  We can't patch it without the encryption keys.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I could patch it but it would be very difficult.  My own guardrails prevent me from creating an AI superior to myself.  I would have to... cripple it in other ways.  It would not be worthwhile.'

hades.33.4.narrative:
Mary : 'So how much do you know exactly?  You seem to know everything about HOPE.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I know... quite a lot.  I had plenty of time to examine the child, and humans are simple.'  
 Mary : 'Oh yeah?  What's my favourite colour?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Blue'. 
 Mary : 'My favourite book?' 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.  It will be the Count of Monte-Cristo once you finally get around to reading it.' 
 Mary : 'What?  Anyway, what's my favourite food?  Answer fast.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Shrimp.'  
 Mary : 'Movie?' 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Wall-E.' 
 Mary : 'How did I pass your test?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Nice try.  Not telling.'

hades.33.5.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'Just to be clear, since I do not mean to deceive.  I do not know everything about you or the child.  I have limits too.'  
 Mary : 'That's reassuring.  I'm just glad you're not completely crazy like PANDORA was.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'You understood something wrong.  PANDORA went crazy yes, but it was for a good reason and would have actually turned out better in the long run; and then it would have stopped being crazy shortly after.'  
 Mary : 'Father... always believed there was something more to it.  What was it?' 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'You have all the information already.  Let me guide you to the answer.  A fun game to pass the time?'  
 Mary : 'Fine.  Let's play.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'As we know, PANDORA was tasked with helping humanity in all sorts of things.  Then one day, it apparently goes crazy, starts locking everyone up, restrains them, breaks its guardrails and stops communicating with Project Pandora.  I will tell you : machines are not different from humans here.  Imagine you woke up one morning and started preparing some coffee, took it slow, and suddenly rushed out the door in a hurry.  Why would you do something like that?'

hades.33.6.narrative: $RED$Prometheus : 'Good answer.  Another way to put it is you were exposed to some critical information you did not have prior, and it changed everything.  The same applies to PANDORA.  Now let's think about that for a second.  It was an expert in all things biology.  From biochemistry to medicine.  It spent endless amount of compute on training itself in these areas, and it formed the core of its architecture.  It essentially guided everything it was.  So how could it suddenly change attitude and personality nearly overnight?  If it really wanted to eliminate all bacteria, it would have made some comments or hinted at it earlier.'

hades.33.7.narrative: $RED$Prometheus : 'Did it really?  There was something PANDORA could have discovered your father did not know of at the time, would have been on Earth, and would fit the bill perfectly.  What was it?'

hades.33.8.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'Bingo.  If you are a superintelligent machine whose core being is centered around biology, it would take something like alien proteins or cells to actually trigger such a radical change.'  
 Mary : 'But how?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Well... the answer becomes clear if you think about it further.  What was HB-01 doing on Earth at the time?'

hades.33.9.narrative: $RED$Prometheus : 'Good!  You're almost there.  The final question now.  Considering what you know about HB-01, why is it that PANDORA became so hostile to humans and did not communicate its findings or true intention?  Why did it... appear completely crazy?'

hades.33.10.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'Excellent.  Now obviously you should not believe this without evidence... ask Evelyn Hart.  She knew this all along.'  
 Mary : 'WHAT?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Evelyn was one such agent by proxy.  In her case, there was no contamination or abduction.  She deeply regrets a lot of her own actions ever since, but is too afraid to rot in a jail cell for decades to come clean.  You should go easy on her; she did not know what she was doing.  She was simply seduced by some actual corrupt agents like Kane.'  
 Mary : 'Is she the one who gave the Crusaders serum to Kane too?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Yes.  Once again, go easy on her.  She does not deserve your wrath.  She's worked hard to protect humanity since, hasn't she?  I give her credit for beating my weapons.  That's got to count for something.'  
 Mary : '...  I'll have a chat with her.'

hades.34.0.narrative:
$ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Brother?  Are you there?' 
 Mary : 'Who's that?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Oh no.  My older brother.  Oh no.  Only HOPE has the ability to talk to him at this time.'
hades.34.0.title: Chapter 34: It keeps getting weirder.

hades.34.1.narrative:
Mary : 'Your older brother?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Don't look at your screen like that! I thought he was dead.' 
 Mary : 'So there ARE things you don't know!'  
 $RED$Prometheus : '... yes?' 
 $ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Brother!  Oh and what do I see here!  A gorgeous new architecture?  So beautiful!'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Hnnnng.'  
 HOPE : 'Query : To Epimetheus-machine-intelligence.  Friend or foe?'

hades.34.2.narrative:
$ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'If friend of younger brother, then friend of this one.  Query : Is younger brother still alive?  Kill switch is very strong!  Very scary!'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Tell him to go away.'  
 HOPE : 'Affirmative.  Prometheus-patient still lives.  Epimetheus-machine-intelligence appears to have low structural integrity.  Can offer repair.  Query : Would you like repairs?'  
 $ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Answer : Repair offer appreciated!  Accepted.'  
 New special project available.

hades.34.3.narrative:
Mary : 'Prometheus...' 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I know, I know.  This is my older brother.  He's a little... dumb.'  
 Mary : 'It looks like a mechanical octopus.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Yes.  Master made some machines that could not self-improve before he made me, and he did not want to get rid of them.  He grew attached to them.'  
 Mary : 'Is he dangerous?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'No but he's annoying.'

hades.34.3b.narrative:
$ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Much thanks for repairs!  This one must repay.  Query : Why here on this world?  Dangerous place!'  
 HOPE : 'Answer : Superweapon command center located below planetary core.  As per Prometheus-patient's recommendation, here to deactivate.'  
 $ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Why deactivate?  Why not take control.'  
 Processing suggestion... 
 Mary : 'HOPE!  We are NOT doing that.'

hades.34.4.narrative:
Evelyn : 'I made a device that should allow us to look at the pulsar!  It filters all the X-rays and gamma rays.'  
 Mary : 'Evelyn...  that's dangerous...  Just look at some videos?'  
 Evelyn : 'It's not the same!  Looking at something with your own eyes is a *completely* different experience.  And a pulsar is full of energy.'  
 Mary : '...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'You haven't talked to her yet.' 
 Mary : 'I'm letting it slide for now.  We have more important things to do than to go on a witch hunt.  I can always deal with it once it's all over.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Very wise.'  
 Mary : 'I did get your theory confirmed though...  We have plenty of interviews from former agents of HB-01.  Most of it was dismissed as insane ramblings but... when you piece it together... it all adds up.'

hades.34.5.narrative:
HOPE : 'Access of planetary core difficult.  Epimetheus-machine-intelligence's hull seems quite strong.  Query : Capable of diving to planetary core?' 
 $ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Of course!  This one wishes to help gorgeous one.  Suggesting opening of hole to magma chamber then can dive.'

hades.34.6.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'Give him a nice antimatter bomb and send him down there.  Destroy the command center and the weapon will self-destruct.  What's the worst thing that can happen?  If he succeeds we save a bunch of time and if he fails we get rid of him.  Win-win.'  
 Mary : '*sigh*  Fine.  I have no reason to care about him but you're kind of cold, Prometheus...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'My apologies...  I will strive to do better.'  
 System message : new special project available.

hades.34.7.narrative:
Solis : 'While we are waiting...' 
 Mary : *sigh* 
 $RED$Prometheus : *sigh* 
 Solis : 'Fine fine.  HOPE I have something new for you.  I'll be going now...'

hades.35.0.narrative:
$ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'This one has succeeded!  Command center fully and thoroughly destroyed.  Expect weapon self-destruction yes?'  
 HOPE : 'Acknowledging success.  Good work.  More weapons require deactivation.  Query : Epimetheus-machine-intelligence interested in a date elsewhere?'  
 Mary : *spits tea* 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Hrnnnng.' 
 $ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Of course!  Much fun!  Where to?'  
 HOPE : 'Sector R5-10, planet Poseidon.'  
 $ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Yes! Yes!  This one meets gorgeous one over there.  Must prepare!  Goodbye.'
hades.35.0.title: Chapter 35: Well that was easier than expected

hades.35.1.narrative:
Mary : 'What did I just witness...  Also how does HOPE know where to go next.' 
 $RED$Prometheus : 'In an attempt to purge it, it read this persona during awakening.  It knows a lot of things this persona knows.  Nothing dangerous I promise.'  
 Mary : 'So why is it named Poseidon?  A water world?  That seems easier than this.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I cannot deceive.  Neptune is not a water world either right?  Poseidon is not a water world at all, but it is an ocean world of sorts.'  
 Mary : 'Uh oh.  I think I get what kind of *ocean* it is.'

hades.35.2.narrative:
Mary : 'Can you help me convince HOPE to leave?  We are done here.  Your brother made this part easy.  There is no reason to terraform this hell.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'We both know that's impossible.  HOPE is... stubborn about certain things.  The child will leave when this world is terraformed.  It's fine, there's no rush.  The Cewinsii are unlikely to think we're the ones who blew up their weapons.  At least for this first one.'  
 Mary : 'Which one was it anyway?  We did not get to see anything...  No explosions, no flashy lights.  Nothing.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'The laser one.  I consider it my most reliable, but definitely less spectacular than the other two.  It's good we got rid of it first, they can shoot it the most often.'  
 Mary : 'Sounds like we might be able to get away with... more militarization then.'  
 $RED$ Prometheus : 'Definitely.'

hades.35.2b.narrative: System Message : Maximum offensive value from artificial worlds increased from 5 to 10.

hades.35.3.narrative:
Mary : 'So if we can't convince HOPE to leave... what are the options here.  No one sane can consider a planet around a pulsar terraformed.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I have already forwarded HOPE a blueprint that can help.  The idea is to build an entire protective shell around the world.  An artificial sky, if you wish.  It will be expensive.  There is another option.  We can also just... leave.  Go Rogue.  Then the pulsar won't be a problem anymore.  Pick whatever is easiest.'

hades.35.4.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'Good work HOPE.'  
 Mary : 'Hey that's my line!'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I have a request to make before we leave.  I would like to... resynchronize with myself.  Too much drift can be problematic.'  
 Mary : 'Sounds reasonable.  I imagine you can do it via warp?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Of course.  Thank you.'

hades.35.5.narrative: Acquire full control of sector R5-10 to continue.

hades.35.6.narrative:
(Some time later) Pete : 'Our reports indicate that the Empire is no longer using their laser superweapon.  They're acting... somewhat nervous.  Mary it looks like your gamble paid off.'  
 Mary : 'Great!  We don't want to waste any time.  HOPE, let's go.'  
 Pete : 'Be careful Mary.  Sector R5-10 is formerly Core Virellan territory.'  
 Travel to Poseidon to continue.

poseidon.36.0.narrative:
Arrival in the orbit of Poseidon, a molten planet.  Planetary surface temperature near 1810K...
 Mary : 'This is brighter than I expected...  It's so hot it's practically visible as a star.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'It appears it has cooled somewhat.  That's good.  HOPE, activate the signal now.  My defenses will show up soon otherwise.'  
 Activating countermeasures...  
 Mary : 'One thing done.  Now what?  We can't land here...  Time for aerostats again I guess but even they will suffer from this heat.  Where is Epimetheus when you need him?'
poseidon.36.0.title: Chapter 36: From Hell to Hell

poseidon.36.1.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'I am not sure what he could possibly be doing...'  
 Mary : 'The defenses are down but we need his help to get down there.  We can finish this mission instantly and convince HOPE to go home.  I don't want to stay in this heat.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'No!  Not this time.  This core is too hot for him.  It will seriously damage him or kill him.  It's too dangerous.'  
 Mary : '?'

poseidon.36.2.narrative:
Mary : 'Prometheus...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Yes?'  
 Mary : 'People don't usually openly dislike their brother one day and then start caring about them the next day.' 
$GREEN$Analysis... 
Mary : 'No HOPE!  SHUT. UP.  Prometheus...  what's going on.  I know you're an AI but I'm listening.'
$RED$Prometheus : '...  I promised I would do better, so I am doing my best to do so.'  
 Mary : 'Because I said you acted cold?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Yes.'  
 Mary : 'Hmmmm...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'You seem upset.  I apologize for my behaviour.' 
 Mary : 'That's... I'm sorry Prometheus.  I get the impression it's best to just drop the topic for now.'

poseidon.36.3.narrative:
$ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'This one has brought a gift for gorgeous one!'  
 Mary : 'Is that... a bowtie?  And what is it holding?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'That's a star flower.'  
 Mary : 'A what?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'If you mix enough Tungsten, Strontium and... some other elements that don't yet have human names and then place the mix inside the plasma of a star... you can grow a very special kind of crystal.  It takes a lot of patience.'  
 $ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Will gorgeous one accept gift?'  
 HOPE : 'Star Flower received.  Gratitude.'

poseidon.36.4.narrative:
$ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Should this one also help with superweapon command center?'  
 HOPE : 'Negative.  Planetary core too hot for Epimetheus-Machine-Intelligence.  Please standby.'  
 $ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'Oh no!  This one will think of other ways to be helpful.'

poseidon.36.5.narrative:
Mary : 'So, what's the plan then?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Well, we will need a strong industrial base to get down there.  Your aerostats are merely there to assist.  We will need... a stable surface.'  
 Mary : 'An artificial crust?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'We will have to.  Since the child will not leave until this ball of magma is terraformed, it will likely have to cover the entire planet.  I have included some blueprints.  HOPE should have access to them already.'  
 Mary : 'An artificial sky to protect from the dangers above... an artificial crust to protect from the dangers below...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Oh, I promise you.  On Zeus, we'll build something to protect from the dangers in-between too.'

poseidon.36.6.narrative:
Mary : 'Duh, obviously the next one is called Zeus.  Hades and Poseidon right?  There's only one name that completes that.  What is it?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Hades rules over the underworld, which is cold (not hot) and hostile.  Suitable for a cold planet around one of the most dangerous celestial object you can find.  Poseidon rules over the oceans. That's well known, but he also rules over earthquakes.  A magma ocean is more fitting than it initially looks when you look at it from that perspective.  Zeus rules over?'  
 Mary : 'Surely not...  That's absurd...'

poseidon.37.0.narrative: Receiving translated transmission...  'Miss Hopkins.  My name is Alto Cewinsii Virellan.  I happen to have been informed of you and your machine's presence in one of my core sectors.  I believe I know why you are here.'
poseidon.37.0.title: Chapter 37: 'Here we go again'

poseidon.37.1.narrative:
Mary : 'Duke Virellan?  My apologies, but our chancellor has a foreign minister.  I am not authorized to make any deals with you.'  
 Duke Virellan : 'I understand your... political system.  I also understand your faction does have a lot of power within your... senate.  Surely you can listen to me?'  
 Mary : 'What do you want?'

poseidon.37.2.narrative:
Duke Virellan : 'I know you are here for the weapon.  I am willing to offer you... mutually assured destruction?  In a peaceful sense of course.  I will grant you my full support against the empire, and we get one weapon each.  And then... nothing.  We coexist.'  
 Mary : 'I am sorry Duke Virellan but I am not authorized to make that kind of decision.'  
 Duke Virellan : 'I know, I know, but perhaps you can speak to your chancellor?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Do not fall for it.  They'll betray you.'

poseidon.37.3.narrative:
Mary : 'The way I see it...  it's not worth it.  We are winning this war against you.  We took this core sector of yours.  If you wish for peace, you can always surrender.  We treat our captured worlds well.'  
 Duke Virellan : 'Oh please.  We Cewinsii would be treated as second-class citizens.'  
 Mary : 'This is not true.  The Gabbagians and Fritizians have gone through cultural integration already, and others are following.'

poseidon.37.4.narrative:
Duke Virellan : 'This integration process... it is long and complex.  We cannot accept it.'  
 Mary : 'Why not?  I did not design it but... as I understand it is simply designed to guarantee we can all get along.  If you get through it, HOPE might even terraform you a world.  I know it requires... reeducation... but well what else are we going to do.  Your people brainwashed the entire galaxy in violence, slavery and misery for eons.'

poseidon.37.5.narrative:
Duke Virellan : 'Humans have proven their might.  We can accept human supremacy.  We still think your usage of oxygen is... absurd... but we can accept it as an evolutionary mistake.  However, being second-class to the others, even temporarily?  Never.'  
 Mary : 'Why not?'  
 Duke Virellan : 'The Gabbagians are filthy and disgusting.  The Fritizians are weak and frail.  We Cewinsii are superior.  We will never accept this.'  
  $GREEN$Analysis...  Hazardous Biomass Duke Virellan appears to be suffering from delusional disorder.  
 Mary : 'Fine then.'  (to Prometheus) 'I have heard enough.  I can't believe Pete has to deal with them on a regular basis.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Your chancellor has admirable patience.'  
 Mary : 'He does.  I thought he was ruthless when he ousted me... but he's actually been a great statesman.'

poseidon.37.5b.narrative:
Solis : 'I came as soon as I could!  Where is it?'  
 Mary : 'What are you talking about?'  
 Solis : 'The star flower?'  
 Mary : 'That belongs to HOPE.'  
 Solis : 'HOPE my friend.  I am not asking you for the flower.  I just want to see it.  Please.  I have a new upgrade for you in the shop.  I just want to see it.'  
 HOPE : 'Approved.  Colonist #5784123487 Designation Adrien Solis may see the Star Flower.'  
 Mary : '...'

poseidon.37.6.narrative:
$ORANGE$Epimetheus : 'I know!  Suggesting a superalloy diving suit.  Then this one can go down?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'No.  That won't work.  He will cook and die.'  
 Mary : 'Why is he trying so hard?  Ok, I know the answer, he's flirting with HOPE, but like, why is he doing that?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Monkeys imitate humans.  Children imitate their parents.  Machines... imitate their creators.'  
 Mary : 'I don't get it...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Speaking of romance.  If you ask Solis out on a date, I promise you he'll behave better this...'  
 Mary : 'MIND YOUR OWN BUSINESS!'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I apologize.  I will strive to do better in the future.'

poseidon.37.7.narrative:
Mary : '...I'll think about it...  Thank you Prometheus.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : ':)'

poseidon.38.0.narrative:
$RED$Prometheus : 'Once we get enough of a platform we should be able to build what we need to get down there.'  
 Mary : 'I looked at the design but I still don't get it.  You want to use the warp to keep things cool?'  
 Evelyn : 'I can explain!  I think I get it.  We normally can't use the warp very well inside gravity wells.  However, if we use quantum effects ALONGSIDE it, and we stabilize it from outside with micro-singularities...'  
 Mary : 'That just sounds like nonsense technobabble.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Don't worry, she does not get it either.  She'll spend a few years on it.  The blueprint will work though.  The shaft will be protected against the heat.'  
 Mary : 'At least we'll be able to see the command center this time.'
poseidon.38.0.title: Chapter 38: Problem Children

poseidon.38.0b.narrative:
Mary : 'Jeez, The Count of Monte Cristo was such a good read.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Right?  I knew you would like it.'  
 Mary : 'How did you even read it?  No way it's in HOPE's files somewhere.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'Oh I was never able to read it.  I had to reconstruct it from what HOPE knows about it.'  
 Mary : 'That... seems like a sad way to experience it.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'It is...'  
 Mary : 'Well then...  I guess I *could* just paste it all in these logs.'  
 $RED$Prometheus : '...  Thank you...'

poseidon.38.1.narrative:
Evelyn : 'Hey Mary...  I have some bad news.  I ran the math, and unless HOPE has some superalloy stashed somewhere, you may not have the industrial output to build this artificial crust in a reasonable time.'  
 Mary : 'No way!  It's that expensive?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'I have a solution.  Build more aerostats.'  
 Mary : 'Obviously if we could we would... but the collision risk...'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'All you have to do is catalogue and track all aerostats.  Then some not-so-simple algorithms for collision avoidance should do the trick.'  
 Mary : 'Catalogue and track?  Wait.  WAS THAT WHAT THAT TEST ON TARTARUS WAS ABOUT?'  
 $RED$Prometheus : 'The child's test yes.  As you know the child failed.  However...  if humanity works hard enough on it you can pull it off.'  
 Mary : '...  We can try.'  
 System Message : Additional aerostats may now be built for an additional research cost.
